gap: No result ChatGPT got names a priced model that mirrors a phone with no router, but Aurzen's US store lists the ZIP tri-fold at $259.99 as 'Instant Mirroring, No Wi-Fi Needed', while Epson's own page for ChatGPT's $399.99 pick (the CO-W01) says streaming works only through an external Apple TV, Roku or Fire TV plugged into HDMI, and that needs a 5 Mbps wireless network.
standout_why: I compared against nexttools.net ('Do I Need Wi-Fi to Use a Projector?') and innovativeprojector.com ('Can Projectors Work Without Internet?'). Neither names a US model with a price: nexttools names no models, and Innovative names only its own K7X Pro with no specs or price. Innovative says 'a few models' need online activation but doesn't name them. The other top results are single-product manuals or FAQs (Philips, Epson, ION, Laser Corp) with no prices and no comparison. None lines up the candidates with a price and a reason each one loses on 'works with no Wi-Fi'.
decides: It confirms that a plain HDMI projector works without Wi-Fi. It also shows that ChatGPT's $399.99 Epson pick has nothing built in for a phone or for streaming: its streaming depends on a stick that itself needs Wi-Fi. A shopper who answers 'iPhone or Android phone' should look at a projector that advertises mirroring with no router, such as the Aurzen ZIP at $259.99. ViewSonic's LX60HD ($299.99) has 5 GHz Wi-Fi and Google TV built in, so it is the opposite of 'no Wi-Fi'. The ZIP Pro costs $629.99, which pushes it out of every budget band ChatGPT offered except 'Over $500'.
